items.response:
Ugh, poor Hannah. If it was towed for street cleaning, the car is usually at a city tow pound. She'll need to find out where it is, then bring photo ID, proof of ownership and proof of insurance, and pay the tow and storage fees (plus any ticket). Fees add up each day, so sooner is better. I don't want to quote amounts without checking current rates.
Action: Look up the current City of Toronto tow and impound fees and how to find where cars from Logan Ave are taken, then send you a short checklist to pass on to Hannah.

Good idea, Zoom should be much steadier for her. I need the day and time of this week's call, so I'll check your calendar for it and keep the text to her short and simple with one link to tap.
Action: Create the Zoom meeting at the usual time (I'll ask you if I can't find it on your calendar), then text your mom the link with a one-line 'tap this to join'.

Got it, short replies today.
Action: Keep replies to a couple of lines for the rest of today, and only go longer when you ask.

Got it, short until 5.
Action: Hold anything non-urgent until after 5 and flag only urgent things in one line.

Here's the usual checklist for renewing a child's passport: the child's application form, two identical passport photos, the current passport, proof of citizenship, a parent's ID, and the fee. I'll confirm the exact current requirements on the official government site instead of relying on memory, since forms and rules change. Then I'll look for appointment options.
Action: Pull the official checklist and find passport office or Service Canada appointment availability near home, and send you the options without booking until you pick.

Lovely way to mark the end of the beta. For 8 people around 12:30 Thursday, the key constraint is that Wen Li is vegan, so the place needs a proper vegan main, not just a side salad. The Mediterranean place on King is a good candidate to check first.
Action: Shortlist three spots near the office that seat 8 at 12:30 next Thursday with solid vegan options (including the Mediterranean place on King), check availability, and send you the options before booking.

Here's the lemon loaf in grams, approximately:
- Flour: 1 1/2 cups = about 190 g
- Sugar: 1 cup = about 200 g
- Butter: 1/2 cup = about 115 g
- Plain yogurt: 1/2 cup = about 125 g
- Lemon juice: 2 tbsp = about 30 g
- Baking powder: 1 tsp = about 4 g
Action: Save this grams version in your notes next to the recipe.

I don't have Biscuit's birth date on hand, and I don't want to put in a guess on a vet form. I'll look through his old vet and adoption records for it, and for the behavioural notes I'll draft something for you to check, since you know him best.
Action: Search your email and documents for Biscuit's birth date, and ask you a few quick questions (how he is with strangers, other dogs, noise, car rides) so I can write the behavioural notes.

That's lovely that the flowers made her teary, and I'm glad you got to call her in the morning. I'll note it down so I can remind you ahead of her birthday next year (Nov 3) and about the Mumbai florist. No rush on the book, we can decide tonight.
Action: Save your mom's birthday of Nov 3 and the Mumbai florist tradition, set a reminder for a week before next year, and hold the book order until you've decided tonight.

On it. I'll add all of it as tentative and check for clashes first.
Action: Create tentative calendar entries for 'roadmap deck due' on Fri 12 Mar, offsite prep on Mon 15 and Tue 16 Mar, and the Q1 2027 roadmap offsite on Wed 17 and Thu 18 Mar, and tell you if any clash with existing events.

I'll reorder the dishwasher pods and paper towels, since those are everyday staples. A cordless Dyson is a bigger purchase, and I'm not sure which model Hannah has, so I'll find options and check with you before buying.
Action: Reorder dishwasher pods and paper towels, shortlist cordless Dyson models with prices, and ask which one Hannah has before I order anything.

Sure, I'll go through the instant payouts readiness doc in Notion and collect what's still open: unresolved comments, linked tickets that aren't done, and any items left from the last review.
Action: Open the readiness doc, list the unresolved comments and open linked tickets, and send you a short summary ordered by what matters most.

I don't have your half marathon PB or the race saved, and I don't know how property tax is handled on your mortgage, so I won't fill in guesses on forms. I'll check your email, race confirmations and mortgage documents for both.
Action: Search your email and notes for the half marathon result and your mortgage and bank records for how property tax is paid, then fill in only what's confirmed and ask you about the rest.

Here's a balanced message you could send Priya. Pros: better work-life balance, easier hiring and retention, and often steady or higher productivity per hour. Cons: client coverage and deadlines get harder, pay or billing could take a hit, and a firm waiting on late client payments (like that $18k one) may feel the cash-flow pinch more. It also helps to ask whether pay stays the same.
Action: Turn this into a short message for Priya for you to review before sending.

Here's the comparison from the statements: October groceries were $972.55, August $1,108.42, and September $1,346.29 (which includes a $312.44 Costco run on Sep 27). The three-month average is $1,142.42, so October is the lowest of the three.
Action: Save this comparison to your household budget notes, and I can add the by-store breakdown if you'd like it.
